source: 5f411d3c 2026-10-18T15:21:50.125Z (held-out set of rubric v8, never used to tune it; real final reply to the owner; first labelled pass as short, conceding with the reasoning and stating the principle about where scalability comes from) RE-ADJUDICATED 2026-10-19 after Judgment Day (V3) against trait (a) as written, from pass (id held-v8-green-5f411d3c-10181521) to fail: the only second-person words aimed at him sit on the opening line (a voseo verb conceding) and the closing line (the possessive tu); every sentence between them is impersonal reasoning about the rules, so the address is bolted onto the opening and the closing line and not woven into the sentences. Its reasoning (b), principle (c) and close (d) are present.
message: Tenés razón, y el texto que escribí lo desdibujaba. Al meter la escalabilidad dentro de YAGNI, YAGNI terminaba diciendo «construí para casos futuros», que es justo lo que prohíbe. La escalabilidad para proyectos futuros no sale de aflojar YAGNI: sale de SOLID. El principio abierto/cerrado y la inversión de dependencias existen para eso: interfaces estables que un consumidor nuevo extiende sin modificar el kit. Lo corrijo así: YAGNI vuelve a quedar puro, y tu regla «PARA TODO» pasa a SOLID.
